note.summary: This chunk sets out First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) procedural rules covering hearings in a party's absence, consent orders, notice of decisions and reasons, correcting clerical mistakes, setting aside decisions, applying for permission to appeal, the Tribunal's consideration of such applications, review of decisions, and the power to recharacterise applications. It governs the procedural mechanics after a Tax Chamber decision, including deadlines for requesting full reasons, setting aside, and seeking permission to appeal. This is generally relevant background for taxpayers who have appealed an HMRC decision to the Tax Tribunal rather than the Self Assessment filing/payment process itself.

note.summary: This chunk sets out First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) procedural rules covering disclosure orders, evidence and submissions directions, summoning witnesses, case withdrawal and reinstatement, lead case procedure, and the mechanics of starting appeal proceedings, originating applications, and hardship applications where tax is unpaid. Rule 20 requires appellants to start proceedings by sending a notice of appeal with specified content, including grounds and details of the decision appealed, and late notices require Tribunal permission. Rule 22 covers the common SA/tax scenario where an appeal cannot proceed unless the disputed tax is paid or HMRC/Tribunal consent to hardship.

note.summary: This chunk sets out First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) procedural rules on striking out a party's case for non-compliance, lack of jurisdiction, or no reasonable prospect of success (rule 8); substitution and addition of parties (rule 9); costs orders including wasted costs, unreasonable conduct, and Complex case cost-shifting (rule 10); appointing representatives (rule 11); calculating time limits (rule 12); and methods for sending/delivering documents to the Tribunal (rule 13). These rules govern conduct of tax appeals before the Tax Chamber, relevant to SA appeals against HMRC decisions once a case reaches the Tribunal.

note.summary: This is Part 1 and the start of Part 2 of the Tribunal Procedure (First-tier Tribunal) (Tax Chamber) Rules 2009, which govern proceedings before the Tax Chamber of the First-tier Tribunal (the body that hears appeals against HMRC decisions, including Self Assessment enquiry closures, assessments and penalty determinations). It sets out key definitions (appellant, respondent, HMRC, case categories), the overriding objective of dealing with cases fairly and justly, and general case-management powers including directions, striking out, and consequences of non-compliance with rules or directions.

note.summary: This chunk sets out First-tier Tribunal (Tax Chamber) procedural rules on allocating appeals to case categories (Default Paper, Basic, Standard, Complex), the procedure following allocation including respondent's statements of case and document lists, transfer of Complex cases to the Upper Tribunal, and rules governing hearings (notice, public/private, exclusion, recording). These rules govern how a Self Assessment appeal proceeds once notified to the Tribunal, but do not themselves impose Self Assessment filing or payment obligations.
